title: AFTER — Concept to Form

body:
Before this I kept saying authorship versus efficiency. Now there is a hand physically reaching back into something the machine changed. That is different.

The wall also helps question 3 finally make more sense. Art might not be a third separate thing sitting beside the project. It can be the place where the other questions happen. Drawing is useful because a finished mark looks simple, but there was a process before it: thinking, movement, hesitation, pressure, changing direction, erasing, maybe explaining why, maybe not knowing why. Then somebody else looks at the final thing and only sees the mark. That is already a form of representation. The AI would be doing something similar. Observing a surface and trying to construct meaning underneath it, which is also where it can be wrong.

I keep thinking about that. If I draw something and somebody says “this represents anger” and I say it does not, does the artist automatically win because it is theirs? Maybe. But people also make things that communicate something they did not consciously intend all the time. Or maybe the viewer is projecting. Or both. That is more interesting to me than an AI that somehow “detects emotion”. The machine makes a claim from what it can observe and then somebody has to deal with the claim existing.

The first version I can actually build needs to be much smaller than the materializations document. A drawing surface, projection maybe, microphone, somebody draws and talks, the system interferes. That is already enough to test something. I do not need VR yet. VR is interesting because making thought spatial could work, but it adds a whole technical project before I know if the actual interaction is even interesting. So delay it. The larger proxy is also later. Anything that requires a fully developed artificial person before the central interaction works is probably backwards. I should prove the interaction first and build the monster around it later if it actually needs the monster.

The authorship hearing is still interesting because it brings public belief back in. Somebody makes a paper with AI involved, AI gradually contributes more, then the human and system both defend why the result belongs to them while other people decide. I still like that because another person's belief can change what authorship means socially even if the person themselves thinks the answer is obvious. But I do not think that should be the first build either. The wall is smaller. That does matter.
I also need to stop making the AI lose on purpose. If it only destroys things, steals things or obviously gets everything wrong then I have already built the answer. It needs to genuinely improve something sometimes. Maybe the participant prefers what it did. Maybe they leave its mark. Maybe they start waiting to see what it suggests. That would be much more uncomfortable than the machine simply ruining their work because now losing some control has something useful attached to it.
“The machine should be helpful.”  I wrote that from the beginning and I still think that is important.

There are still assumptions everywhere though. I assume people care about authorship. Some people genuinely might not. I assume they will resist the machine when it gets something wrong. Some might just accept it. I assume university students understand AI enough to notice what is happening, but maybe knowing too much about AI changes how they interact with it. I assume spending more time with someone makes the machine more “them”, but how much time is enough? Five minutes, thirty minutes, weeks? That completely changes what I could claim the system knows.

I also have not done enough outside research with actual people yet. Working alone is good because I can finally let the project become specifically mine without constantly turning it into something multiple people need to agree with. But it is also dangerous because one person (me) can keep proving themselves right forever. I need people telling me when my concept stops making sense.

And I need a physical test. That is the biggest thing that is not up to standard right now. The materialization assignment has forms, maquettes, interactions and writing, but it does not have a participant interacting with any real system. So I still do not know whether close actually feels like anything.

I keep writing “close is how the line blurs”. Okay. Then I need to build close.

What does that mean technically? If the machine changes a drawing slightly, maybe nobody cares. If it changes too much it is obviously not theirs anymore. Somewhere in between there might be a moment where the participant hesitates before deleting it. That hesitation might tell me more than another ten pages about identity.

The research is also still behind the concept. I have enough source names. I do not have enough depth. Question 1 is still enormous. Question 2 still contains resemblance, efficiency, authorship, dependence and agency. Question 3 might stop being a separate question and become a method. I do not think I need to solve all of that right now, but I do need to stop making the physical project bigger while the thinking underneath it is still thin.

What I think is actually in the centre now is identity, authorship and displacement of the self through an external system observing and acting. AI puts pressure on that. Art gives me somewhere for it to happen. Efficiency is why somebody might allow it to happen.

And I still do not want the piece telling people what conclusion to reach. Maybe somebody comes out thinking the AI made their work better and they genuinely do not care which marks were theirs. That is allowed. Maybe someone hates every intervention. Also allowed. Maybe someone cannot decide. That is probably more interesting. If I already know what the correct answer is then I do not really know why I would make the installation.

The sentence I am still sitting with now is: If something can help me say, make or do what I was already trying to do, at what point am I still being extended and at what point have I just made myself less necessary?

I still do not know where that point is. That might actually be the project.
